CRI / KETAMINE

Ketamine CRI

Uses the shared species and weight above. Workbook profiles & clinical references.

Best use: Adjunct to opioid analgesia when pain control is inadequate; reassess comfort and adverse effects. Veterinary reference.

Prepare an infusion

Workbook analgesic options: 0.1–0.6 mg/kg/hr; select the prescribed dose.

Run time changes the amount prepared, not the prescribed dose. Changing the pump input calculates a new preparation; it does not titrate an existing syringe. Duration is nominal before priming/discard.

More info · concentration reference

Concentration reference

Assumed stock: 100 mg/mL. Workbook preparation options: 1, 5 or 10 mg/mL; default 10. These are workbook choices, not universal veterinary maximums. Product formulations differ; the linked human Ketalar label requires dilution of its 100 mg/mL product before IV administration.

Stock is the vial concentration; prepared concentration is what reaches the pump. Verify the actual vial and local preparation protocol.

Practice source

Merck Veterinary Manual · veterinary clinical reference. Best-use wording is a clinical summary, not a complete treatment protocol.
